summary: Priming cache starvation causing early client timeouts on very large max_tokens requests
description:
Issue summary:
Customers on Dedicated capacity (NoteApp Inc.) observe client-side timeouts when requesting very large max_tokens (>= 150k) together with an extensive system/user prompt (large prefix). The request appears to make progress (streamed chunks arrive), then stalls during a late-stage KV priming operation and the client aborts after its timeout.

Impact:
- NoteApp reports 12% of large-output requests failing with client timeouts over the last 24h (prod us-east).
- Affects both streaming and non-streaming flows for long-context prompts.
- Customer experiencing increased error budget and user-facing failures.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: dp-us-east-2 (3x A100 nodes reserved).
- Serving runtime: release v4.8.1 (kernel selection heuristics updated in v4.8.0).
- Observed primarily on models listed above.

Steps to reproduce (from customer):
1) Create long system prompt ~120k tokens (multiple docs + metadata).
2) Issue generate request with max_tokens=160000, streaming=true, timeout client-side=90s.
3) Observe initial streaming chunks for ~40s, then a long pause (~50s) and finalization never finishes before client timeout -> client aborts with ECONNRESET.

Observed logs/metrics:
- Serving logs show a spike in finalizer queue depth and KV cache reloads at the time of the requests (see grafana panels).
- CPU on GPU-hosts spikes for the priming thread; GPU utilization remains moderate indicating a blocking CPU-bound operation.
- No 5xx from API gateway; we return partial stream frames then stall.
- Customer trace id samples: trace-us-east-ff21a0, trace-us-east-eb33c2.

Customer-provided artifacts:
- Request payload (redacted) attached in customer portal (ref: noteapp-req-20260311-17).
- Client logs showing ECONNRESET and duration ~90s.

Temporary workaround suggested to customer:
- Reduce max_tokens to <= 80k or split generation into smaller chained calls.
- Disable large-context KV priming by setting prompt_chunking=false (if feasible) — customer accepted short-term workaround.

investigation_notes: Hypothesis: When prefix tokens + max_tokens crosses combined threshold, the runtime eagerly serializes large KV blocks into memory which runs on main priming thread causing blocking behavior.
Perf traces show priming step accounts for ~60-70% of elapsed time during stalled period; GC pressure increases concurrently.
Reproducer on dedicated staging shows identical finalizer queue spikes when we simulate same prefix sizes and token budgets.
Lock profiling points to kv-serializer mutex (hot path) where several worker threads queue up; moving to per-shard serialization reduced contention in local experiments.
Related to recent kernel-selection heuristics change in v4.8.0 that changed priming ordering and made more eager KV assembly for predicted completion ordering.
resolution: Workaround: customer to limit max_tokens or split requests; engineering to merge non-blocking priming patch that defers heavy KV serialization and applies a cap on synchronous priming. PR 489 under review; plan to ship hotfix to dedicated fleet and notify customer. Postmortem to cover thresholds and add telemetry for priming queue depth.
